title: I challenged Gawain Jones!
transcript: This is me, a 1700 rated player, and my opponent is the three times British champion in Grandmaster Gawway Jones. The game starts with a London system, and since I had warned him before the [music] game that I was going to play this, he goes for a Kings Indian setup to counter it, and I decide to attack the king's side right away. Very soon in the game, he picks up a pawn, but the game is still in the balance. I attack the queen and I force it to move to the other side of the board. And now I decide to But this is where Gane makes a mistake. He attacks my knight. But [music] after I move my knight, now there are going to be two pawns hanging. Don't tell me it's >> But I do see it. I attack the queen to misplace it. And this is where Gane starts to hesitate. He knows that he wants to move the queen, but he doesn't know where to. >> He eventually moves the queen to E7. [music] And now I have a chance to go for the win if I find the move knight D to B5. Instead, I go for the simpler capture of the pawn. But believe it or not, Gane here blunders a full rook and he notices right away. But I am too focused on the [music] threats on my king. So I move that and that gives him a chance to fix his mistake. [laughter] I am now out of luck and gain starts to win the game. [laughter] >> Eventually he attacks [music] both of my rooks and I blunder one of them determining the end of the game.
